text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

text: The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku's card stays face down.
The game is over. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the officer, Haiku the doctor, Gemma the citizen, Sol the citizen, Luna the killer, Terra the killer.

Haiku claimed to be a plain citizen and spent day one pressing Sonnet and Sol, while Luna backed Haiku's questions. Sonnet, the officer, hinted at Luna with timing talk instead of claiming the role, and the town voted Sonnet out on day one. Sol was killed the next night, after backing that vote. On day two Haiku turned on the clean citizen Gemma, then dropped Terra, and Luna and Terra voted Haiku out. Two killers outnumbered the lone citizen left standing, so the killers won.
